ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a human reviewer: confirm whether the 14:59–15:05 segment can be tied to the consented Bukit Batok West Avenue 3 route; if it cannot, refund 1.82 km × $1.4101/km = $2.57 (voucher) on top of the already-admitted $3.71 for 15:16–15:23.
ruling.reasoning: RydeTAXI is metered, so extra kilometres on an unexempted off-route segment flow into the fare and are refundable at this trip's distance rate, $33.56 ÷ 23.80 km = $1.4101/km [F5][F8][RD-2].
ruling.escalation_reason: segment finding undetermined for F3; evidence insufficient: No record ties the 14:59–15:05 off-route segment [F3] to the road the rider agreed to (Bukit Batok West Avenue 3, [F9][F10]): the chat holds only two messages with no road name or location placing the car on that road for this segment, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F11]. The trace also marks the RD-4(a) incident screen as no-evidence for this segment, so the segment's exemption status cannot be settled by the record.

segment_findings.reason: Chat #1 at 14:56 asks 'can I go round via Bukit Batok West Avenue 3?' and Chat #2 at 14:56 answers 'Sure, no problem.' — a rider message sent before the 14:59 segment start, naming a specific road [F9][F10][F3][F11]. Under RD-5 that consent covers driving on Bukit Batok West Avenue 3 only, and the record must tie the driven stretch to that road; the chat carries no road name or location for the driven path and no stop places the car there, so timing alone cannot establish the tie and the finding is undetermined (G13), not exempt [RD-5]. RD-3(a) does not exempt it either: the rider named a road, not a stop, and no stop was measured in this segment [RD-3]. RD-4(a) fails: no incident on the replaced stretch and speed band alone does not exempt [F15][RD-4]. This finding changes the amount, so it goes to a person.

The 15:16–15:23 segment adds 2.63 km [F4]. The last rider message is at 14:56, before this segment began, and no rider message agrees to this stretch; the driver's own post-trip statement attributes the second turn-off to 'my GPS rerouting', not to any rider request [F10][F11][F12]. A driver's claim of agreement in his statement is not consent (G11), and RD-3(a) gives no cover because no rider-named stop exists here [RD-5][RD-3]. RD-4 offers no reasonable-cause defence: no incident was recorded near the route and the only band evidence is band 4 on the PIE, which under RD-4(b) is corroboration at most and cannot exempt on its own [F13][F15][RD-4]. The segment is therefore an unexempted deviation refundable under RD-2: 2.63 km × $1.4101/km = $3.7086 → $3.71 [F4][F5][RD-2].
